summary: Iter8 retest of VerifyEmail.jsx StrictMode fix — FAILED. The fix regressed the bug from 'shows verify-error' to 'stuck forever on Verifying… spinner' (neither verify-success nor verify-error renders). Backend verification is 100% correct (POST /api/auth/verify-email returns 200 {ok:true}, /api/auth/me returns email_verified=true, xp=30 — 5 login-streak + 25 verify bonus). The single-shot useRef guard stops the second POST but the first effect's cleanup still flips `cancel=true` before the first POST's response arrives, and `if (cancel) return` aborts the setState('success') call. Net result: loading state never resolves.

ui_bugs.issue: After the StrictMode fix, valid-token verify is stuck on 'Verifying…' forever. Neither data-testid='verify-success' nor data-testid='verify-error' is rendered. Network confirms POST /auth/verify-email → 200 {ok:true}. The bug is that the useEffect's cleanup runs between StrictMode's first and second invocation and sets cancel=true; the async POST resolves AFTER cleanup, so the `if (cancel) return;` guard on line 26 (and line 31) aborts the setState('success'). The single-shot sentRef guard correctly prevents the second POST but does not address the cancel-flag race.

action_items: Fix VerifyEmail.jsx: remove the `cancel` flag OR do not set cancel=true in the cleanup when sentRef is already set (StrictMode second-pass cleanup). Simplest correct fix: drop the `let cancel = false;` + `if (cancel) return;` pattern entirely (the sentRef guard already makes the effect idempotent), OR use a module-scoped Map<token, Promise> cache so both StrictMode passes await the same in-flight request. Concretely in useEffect: remove lines 22, 26, 31, 57-59 (cancel variable, the two if(cancel) returns, and the cleanup return). Current StrictMode behaviour: run1 → sentRef=true, async POST starts → cleanup1 sets cancel1=true → run2 early-returns (fresh cancel2=false unused) → POST resolves but cancel1===true so setState never fires → user is stuck on the spinner forever with no recourse (no Continue button, no Go back button).
critical_code_review_comments: /app/frontend/src/pages/VerifyEmail.jsx:15-60 — the useRef single-shot guard is correct for preventing the duplicate POST, but the unchanged `let cancel = false` + cleanup → `cancel = true` pattern now aborts the happy-path setState in StrictMode (first cleanup fires BEFORE the single POST resolves). Because sentRef makes the effect idempotent, the cancel flag is both unnecessary AND actively harmful here. Recommend removing it entirely.

Minor: even with a correct fix, the fallback path at line 34 `if (user?.email_verified)` will almost always be false on the verify page because the user hasn't been refreshed yet. The /auth/me fallback at line 40-46 is the one that actually runs — consider hoisting it to the main success path or just rely on the backend response for a cleaner flow.
Minor: line 60 `eslint-disable-line` comment is disabling the exhaustive-deps warning for `user`/`refresh` dependencies — acceptable here but worth a comment.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Reproduce: (1) POST /api/auth/register with any new email → get JWT + user. (2) mongosh: db.email_verification_tokens.find({email:<e>,used:false}).sort({created_at:-1}).limit(1) → extract .token. (3) localStorage.setItem('skiller_token', <jwt>) in Playwright. (4) goto /verify-email/<token>. (5) Network panel will show POST /auth/verify-email → 200 {ok:true}, but UI stays on 'Verifying…'. The `cancel` flag pattern in the useEffect is what's breaking it under StrictMode — the cleanup fires after the first run but before the POST resolves. Testing from this agent confirmed: email_verified=true and xp=30 via /api/auth/me, so backend is perfect. Only the UI state transition is broken.
rca of the issue: React 18 StrictMode invokes each effect twice in dev: run → cleanup → run. VerifyEmail.jsx uses a useRef single-shot guard to block the second POST, which works. BUT the first effect's cleanup still sets a closure-scoped `cancel = true`, and both `if (cancel) return` branches inside the async function (lines 26 and 31) now trigger on the original Promise resolution. The setState('success') at line 27 is skipped; the component never leaves 'loading'. Mitigation: delete the `cancel` local variable and the cleanup return, since sentRef already provides idempotency; OR guard with `if (sentRef.current && !settledRef.current) setState(...)` pattern; OR cache the in-flight Promise in a module-level Map keyed by token so both StrictMode passes share a single resolution.
